title: Unified Decision Flywheel: feature discovery plus few-shot optimization
description:
## Purpose

Show, with small fast Jev experiments, that one flywheel doing **both** optimizations ends in a fixed, reloadable classifier bundle that is at least as good as either lever alone.

## Product definition (owner, 2026-10-01)

- **One flywheel, two optimizations** from labeled human feedback, comments included: (1) **feature discovery**: an analyst turns explanations and errors into new rubric questions (as in Jev-Flywheel); (2) **few-shot optimization**: a native optimizer iteratively improves one **fixed** example list.
- **End state:** a fixed classifier bundle = optimized fixed example list + discovered rubric questions + trained ML head over Jev answers (1 Jev request per item: the example list in the state together with every rubric question; owner, Q2).
- **Dynamic per-item retrieval is a separate, optional feature, off by default** (and stays off by default regardless of benchmark results, because it is harder to deploy; owner, Q3), with configurable retrievers: lexical (stop words on by default), in-memory embeddings as the simplest semantic option, and S3 Vectors / DynamoDB vector search behind the same interface (design only for now).
- Native, provider-neutral optimization. No DSPy.

## Owner constraints

- Small fast experiments: 100–200 labels per round, an afternoon, a few dollars.
- **Jev spending is pre-approved within the design caps:** one new cumulative ledger ceiling of **7,500 Jev requests, ≈$4** (design §5, §5.3). Anything beyond needs new approval.
- Laya and Kev cannot do few-shot; they are not in this phase.

## Phasing (owner)

- **Phase 1:** fixed-list policy, optimizer, harness arms F / F-rand, first live reading (≈$0.55). Stops S0–S1.
- **Phase 2:** explanation labeler, feature discovery with comments, bundle save/load, rounds 2–3, final paper-600 through reloaded bundles. Stops S3–S5.
- **Phase 3:** lexical v2, embedding retriever, AWS store designs; free retrieval proxy first (S2), at most one live D variant.

The design's build order (§6) places the retrieval proxy (S2) before the labeler (S3); the owner's phasing moves it to Phase 3. Stop-point names follow the design.

## Owner decisions (2026-10-01)

- Q1 explanation evidence: a simulated human consulting its own hidden rubric (as in Jev-Flywheel's recorded simulated-labeler); real datasets later. decision-flywheel-evaluations-81f0ec6c-0714-4f22-8725-9bd0bf4e4b94
- Q2 request shape: one Jev request per item, examples in the state with every rubric question; cache key includes the list fingerprint. decision-flywheel-evaluations-5e067f89-04ba-4b0e-84b3-09ae93c8127b
- Q3 default: the fixed list, regardless of any retrieval result; retrieval comparisons are only reported. decision-flywheel-evaluations-b22370aa-0cf1-4b8c-8590-05ea3128fc7c
- Design §7 Q4–Q7 (porting `Score`/`fit_head` into core, embedding default for customer data, Jev model pinning, labels per round) remain open in the design and are not assumed.

## Definition of done

S5 reached: frozen bundles scored on paper-600 **through reloaded bundles**, a one-page result in `studies/` with paired intervals, actual spend and L2 caveats, and each §5.4 design consequence applied or explicitly deferred by the owner.

## Sources

- Design: [DECISION_FLYWHEEL_DESIGN.md](https://github.com/AnthusAI/Decision-Flywheel-Evaluations/blob/main/studies/DECISION_FLYWHEEL_DESIGN.md)
- First experiment: [UNIFIED_FLYWHEEL_PLAN.md](https://github.com/AnthusAI/Decision-Flywheel-Evaluations/blob/main/studies/UNIFIED_FLYWHEEL_PLAN.md), [UNIFIED_FLYWHEEL_RESULTS.md](https://github.com/AnthusAI/Decision-Flywheel-Evaluations/blob/main/studies/UNIFIED_FLYWHEEL_RESULTS.md)
- Supersedes the priority of `decision-flywheel-evaluations-049a2c8b-1798-5cf5-8a81-3cda98d0f924` (static, ordering and cross-model plan). The static study is complete: [INITIAL_JEV_RESULTS.md](https://github.com/AnthusAI/Decision-Flywheel-Evaluations/blob/main/studies/INITIAL_JEV_RESULTS.md).
